extracted.intended_audience: air carriers/operators and their compliance/officer staff responsible for aircraft water systems (also FAA/EPA inspectors)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and operational standards air carriers must follow for monitoring, disinfecting, sampling, notifying, reporting, recordkeeping, inspections, and supplemental treatment of aircraft water systems under the Revised Total Coliform Rule (Subpart Y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain routine monitoring when all samples negative
rubrics_metrics.description: If all routine sample results are total coliform-negative, then the air carrier must maintain the routine monitoring frequency for total coliform as specified in the sampling plan in § 141.802.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective actions for any routine E. coli-positive sample
rubrics_metrics.description: If any routine sample is E. coli-positive, the air carrier must perform all of the following:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Restrict public access in accordance with paragraph (d) as expeditiously as possible, but no later than 24 hours after laboratory notification; restrictions and public notifications remain until system disinfected/flushed and a complete set of follow-up samples is total coliform-negative. (ii) Disinfect and flush in accordance with § 141.804(b)(2); if system cannot be physically disconnected/shut-off or flow prevented, disinfect/flush no later than 72 hours after lab notification. (iii) Collect follow-up samples per paragraph (e); a complete set of follow-up sample results must be total coliform-negative before providing water for human consumption and returning to routine monitoring frequency per § 141.802.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective options for routine total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative
rubrics_metrics.description: If any routine sample is total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative, the air carrier must perform at least one of the following three corrective actions and continue that action until a complete set of follow-up or repeat samples is total coliform-negative:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Disinfect and flush per § 141.804(b)(2) no later than 72 hours after lab notification; then collect follow-up samples per paragraph (e) prior to providing water; must be total coliform-negative before returning to routine frequency. (ii) Restrict public access per paragraph (d) no later than 72 hours after lab notification, conduct disinfection and flushing per § 141.804(b)(2), then collect follow-up samples per paragraph (e) prior to providing water; must be total coliform-negative before returning to routine frequency. (iii) Repeat sampling: collect three 100 mL repeat samples no later than 24 hours after lab notification from specified taps (positive tap, one other lavatory tap, one other galley tap; if fewer than three taps, collect from available taps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes of repeat sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: If repeat samples are collected following a total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative routine result, then:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) If all repeat samples are total coliform-negative, maintain routine monitoring frequency per § 141.802. (B) If any repeat sample is E. coli-positive, perform all corrective actions specified in paragraphs (c)(2)(i), (c)(2)(ii), and (c)(2)(iii) (E. coli corrective actions). (C) If any repeat sample is total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative, perform the corrective actions specified in paragraphs (c)(3)(i) or (c)(3)(ii) (coliform corrective actions) and continue until a complete set of follow-up samples is total coliform-negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of public access defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction of public access to the aircraft water system includes specific measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include (1) physically disconnecting or shutting off the aircraft water system, or otherwise preventing flow through taps; (2) providing public notification to passengers and crew per § 141.805; (3) providing alternatives such as bottled water for drinking and coffee/tea preparation, antiseptic hand gels or wipes in galleys and lavatories (per 21 CFR part 333), and other feasible measures to reduce/eliminate use of the aircraft water system until unrestricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-disinfection and flushing follow-up sampling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Following corrective action disinfection and flushing, air carriers must comply with follow-up sampling procedures that, at a minimum, include:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) For each aircraft water system, collect a complete set of total coliform follow-up samples consisting of two 100 mL total coliform samples at the same routine sample locations identified in paragraphs (b)(2) and (b)(4). (2) Collect follow-up samples prior to providing water for human consumption. (3) If a complete set is total coliform-negative, return to routine monitoring frequency per § 141.802. (4) If any follow-up sample is E. coli-positive, perform E. coli corrective actions per paragraphs (c)(2)(i)-(iii). (5) If any follow-up sample is total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative, restrict public access per paragraph (d) no later than 72 hours after lab notification, disinfect/flush per § 141.804(b)(2), collect follow-up samples per paragraph (e), and ensure complete set is total coliform-negative before resuming public water use and routine frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to perform routine disinfection/flushing or collect routine samples
rubrics_metrics.description: If the air carrier fails to perform routine disinfection and flushing or fails to collect and analyze the required number of routine coliform samples, the air carrier must perform all the corrective actions as specified in paragraph (c)(3)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (c)(3)(ii) refers to restricting public access and subsequent disinfection/flushing and follow-up sampling as described for total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to collect repeat or follow-up samples
rubrics_metrics.description: If the air carrier fails to collect and analyze the required follow-up samples as a result of an E. coli-positive result, then the air carrier must perform all corrective actions as specified in paragraphs (c)(2)(i)-(iii). If the air carrier fails to collect and analyze the required repeat samples or follow-up samples as a result of a total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative result, then the air carrier must perform all corrective actions as specified in paragraph (c)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective actions when unsafe boarding causes E. coli-positive
rubrics_metrics.description: For the aircraft water system, the air carrier must perform all the corrective actions specified in paragraphs (c)(2)(i)-(iii) when it becomes aware of an E. coli-positive event resulting from:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Boarding water from a watering point not in accordance with FDA regulations (21 CFR part 1240 subpart E). (2) Boarding water that does not meet NPDWRs applicable to transient non-community water systems (§§ 141.62 and 141.63, as applied to TNCWS). (3) Boarding water otherwise determined unsafe due to non-compliance with procedures specified in § 141.804(b)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective actions when unsafe boarding causes non-E. coli-positive event
rubrics_metrics.description: For the aircraft water system, the air carrier must perform all corrective actions specified in paragraph (c)(3)(ii) when it becomes aware of a non-E. coli-positive event resulting from:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Boarding water not in accordance with FDA regulations (21 CFR part 1240, subpart E). (2) Boarding water that does not meet NPDWRs applicable to TNCWS (§§ 141.62 and 141.63). (3) Boarding water otherwise unsafe due to non-compliance with § 141.804(b)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations and maintenance plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each air carrier must develop and implement an aircraft water system operations and maintenance plan for each aircraft water system that it owns or operates; this plan must be included in an FAA-accepted air carrier operations and maintenance program (14 CFR part 43, 14 CFR part 91, 14 CFR part 121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Watering point selection requirement in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: All watering points must be selected in accordance with Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations (21 CFR part 1240, subpart E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement must be included in the operations and maintenance plan for each aircraft water system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection and flushing procedures in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include procedures for disinfection and flushing of aircraft water systems including requirements that:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) The air carrier must conduct disinfection and flushing in accordance with, or consistent with, the water system manufacturer's recommendations; may conduct more frequently but not less frequently than manufacturer recommends. (ii) The plan must identify disinfection frequency, type of disinfecting agent, disinfectant concentration, disinfectant contact time, and flushing volume or flushing time. (iii) If manufacturer doesn't specify a routine frequency, the carrier must choose disinfection/flushing and monitoring frequency specified in § 141.803(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan must include follow-up sampling procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The operations and maintenance plan must include the procedures for follow-up sampling in accordance with § 141.803(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Training for all personnel involved with aircraft water system operation and maintenance must include, but is not limited to:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Boarding water procedures; (ii) Sample collection procedures; (iii) Disinfection and flushing procedures; (iv) Public health and safety reasons for the requirements of this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-inspection procedures in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The operations and maintenance plan must include procedures for conducting self-inspections of the aircraft water system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must include inspection of storage tank, distribution system, supplemental treatment, fixtures, valves, and backflow prevention devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boarding water procedures in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include requirements and procedures for boarding water including:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Within the United States, board water from watering points in accordance with FDA regulations (21 CFR part 1240, subpart E). (ii) A description of how water will be transferred from the watering point to the aircraft to ensure it will not become contaminated during transfer. (iii) A description of how the carrier will ensure that water boarded outside the United States is safe for human consumption. (iv) A description of emergency procedures that meet requirements in § 141.803(h) and (i) to be used if water was boarded from non-compliant/unsafe watering points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coliform sampling plan inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must include the coliform sampling plan prepared in accordance with § 141.802 in the operations and maintenance plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disconnect/shut-off statement in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The operations and maintenance plan must include an explanation of whether the aircraft water system can be physically disconnected/shut-off, or the flow of water otherwise prevented through the tap(s) to the crew and passengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for developing operations and maintenance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: For existing aircraft, the plan must be developed by April 19, 2011; for new aircraft, within the first calendar quarter of initial operation of the aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any changes to the operations and maintenance plan must be included in the FAA-accepted air carrier operations and maintenance program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations requiring public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Air carriers must give public notice for each aircraft in the situations listed (e.g., restrictions due to routine/repeat/follow-up total coliform-positive or E. coli-positive; failure to perform required routine disinfection/flushing or monitoring; failure to collect required follow-up/repeat samples; events from boarding unsafe water; other determinations that notification is necessary to protect public health).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 141.805(a)(1)-(7) for full situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General public notification formatting and language requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notifications must meet formatting and language standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications: (1) Must be displayed conspicuously when printed or posted; (2) Must not contain overly technical language or very small print; (3) Must not be formatted in a way that defeats purpose; (4) Must not contain language that nullifies purpose; (5) Must contain information in appropriate language(s) and reflect good faith effort to reach non-English speaking population, including an easily recognized symbol for non-potable water where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification content for restriction due to positive sample (paragraph a(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notification must include prominently displayed, clear statement in each lavatory that the water is non-potable and must include a prominent galley notice directed at the crew containing specific items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galley notice must include: (i) clear statement water is non-potable; (ii) description of the violation or situation triggering the notice including contaminant(s); (iii) when the violation/situation occurred; (iv) any potential adverse health effects (per paragraph (g)); (v) population at risk including sensitive subpopulations; (vi) what the air carrier is doing to correct the violation; (vii) when the air carrier expects to return the system to unrestricted public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-notice exception when access physically prevented
rubrics_metrics.description: If passenger access is physically prevented (system disconnected/shut-off or flow prevented or water supplied only to lavatory toilets), then only the galley/crew notice specified in (c)(2) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air carriers must initiate public notification when restriction of public access is initiated and continue until system returned to unrestricted access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification content for failures and non-E. coli events (paragraphs a(2), (a)(4), (a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notification must meet general requirements and include lavatory non-potable statement and a prominent galley notice with content specific to these situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galley notice must include: (i) clear non-potable statement; (ii) clear statement that it is not known whether water is contaminated because of failure to perform required actions or monitoring or boarding from non-compliant watering point; (iii) when and where unsafe water was boarded or when requirement not met; (iv) potential adverse health effects (per paragraph (g)); (v) population at risk including sensitive subpopulations; (vi) statement indicating when system will be disinfected/flushed and returned to unrestricted access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification content for contamination or monitoring failure (paragraphs a(3), (a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notification must meet general requirements and include lavatory non-potable statement and a prominent galley notice with content specific to contamination or monitoring failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galley notice must include: (i) clear non-potable statement; (ii) clear statement that the water is contaminated and there was failure to conduct required monitoring or water was boarded from a non-compliant watering point; (iii) description of contaminant(s) of concern; (iv) when and where unsafe water was boarded or when monitoring requirement was not met; (v) potential adverse health effects (per paragraph (g)); (vi) population at risk including sensitive subpopulations; (vii) statement indicating what the air carrier is doing to correct situation; (viii) when the air carrier expects to return the system to unrestricted access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification initiation and delivery methods for Administrator-required notices (paragraph a(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification must be in form and manner reasonably calculated to reach all passengers and crew while on board using one or more delivery methods and must be initiated within timing specified by EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred delivery methods include: (i) broadcast over public announcement system on aircraft; (ii) posting notices in conspicuous locations (normally galleys and lavatories); (iii) hand delivery to passengers and crew; (iv) another delivery method approved in writing by the Administrator. Air carriers must initiate public notification within 24 hours of being informed by EPA to perform notification and continue notification for the duration determined by EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard health effects language templates for crew notices
rubrics_metrics.description: In each public notice to the crew, air carriers must use prescribed standard health effects language corresponding to different triggering situations (total coliform only, any E. coli-positive, failures to monitor/disinfect, failures to follow-up after E. coli-positive or contaminated boarding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates include: (g)(1) language for coliform-only detection explaining coliforms as indicator organisms and possible short-term health effects and higher risk to infants, young children, elderly, immunocompromised; (g)(2) E. coli language indicating contamination with human/animal wastes and possible short-term health effects and vulnerable populations; (g)(3) language when required monitoring/disinfection not conducted explaining uncertainty and potential health effects; (g)(4) language for failure to conduct required follow-up after E. coli-positive or when water boarded contaminated with E. coli, including wording alternatives provided in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting development of plans and frequencies (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Air carriers must report to the Administrator that they have developed the coliform sampling plan and the operations and maintenance plan and report the frequencies for routine coliform sampling and routine disinfection and flushing by specified deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For existing aircraft: report by April 19, 2011. For each new aircraft: report within the first calendar quarter of initial operation. Reports must cover each aircraft water system and identified frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting inventory and inventory changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must report a complete inventory of aircraft that are public water systems by April 19, 2011 and report changes in inventory no later than 10 days following the calendar month in which the change occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory must include at least: (i) unique aircraft identifier number; (ii) status (active or inactive) as an aircraft water system; (iii) type and location of any supplemental treatment equipment installed; (iv) whether the system can be physically disconnected/shut-off or flow prevented. Changes include new/removed aircraft identifiers, status changes, changes to supplemental equipment, and changes to disconnectability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting sampling results and disinfection events
rubrics_metrics.description: All sampling results must be reported no later than 10 calendar days following the monitoring period in which the sampling occurred. Routine disinfection and flushing events must be reported no later than 10 calendar days following the disinfection and flushing period in which the event occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monitoring and disinfection/flushing periods are based on frequencies identified in the coliform sampling plan (§ 141.802) and operations and maintenance plan (§ 141.804).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting events requiring notification and failures
rubrics_metrics.description: All events requiring notification to passengers or crew, non-routine disinfection and flushing, or non-routine sampling must be reported within 10 days of the event. Failure to comply with monitoring or disinfection and flushing requirements must be reported within 10 calendar days of discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting changes to frequencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in disinfection and flushing and coliform sampling frequencies must be reported no later than 10 days following the calendar month in which the change occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to routine coliform sampling frequency and routine disinfection and flushing frequency must be included in the aircraft water system operations and maintenance plan that is included in the FAA-accepted program per § 141.804.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic reporting requirement and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: All information required to be reported to the Administrator under this subpart must be in an electronic format established or approved by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an air carrier is unable to report electronically, the air carrier may use an alternative approach that the Administrator approves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-inspection reporting and deficiency reporting timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must provide evidence of a self-inspection to the Administrator within 90 days of completion of the self-inspection required under § 141.808(b), including reporting whether all deficiencies were addressed per § 141.808(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any deficiency has not been addressed within 90 days of identification, the report must include a description of the deficiency, an explanation why it has not yet been addressed, and a schedule for addressing it as expeditiously as possible. Also must report that any deficiency identified during a compliance audit has been addressed within 90 days or include the same detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for bacteriological analyses (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep records of bacteriological analyses for at least 5 years including specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include: (1) date, time, and place of sampling, and name of person who collected the sample; (2) identification of the sample as routine, repeat, follow-up, or other special purpose; (3) date of the analysis; (4) laboratory and person responsible for performing the analysis; (5) analytical technique/method used; (6) results of the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for disinfection and flushing (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep records of any disinfection and flushing for at least 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include: (1) date and time of the disinfection and flushing; and (2) the type of disinfection and flushing (i.e., routine or corrective action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for self-inspections (10 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep records of a self-inspection for at least 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include the completion date of the self-inspection and copies of any written reports, summaries, or communications related to the self-inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sampling plans and O&M plans available for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must maintain sampling plans and aircraft water system operations and maintenance plans and make such plans available for review by the Administrator upon request, including during compliance audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations and maintenance plans must be maintained in accordance with FAA requirements and included in FAA-accepted programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of public notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep copies of public notices to passengers and crew issued as required by this subpart for at least 3 years after issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator audits and compliance audits scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may conduct routine compliance audits as necessary to ensure proper implementation of the subpart; compliance audits may include specified activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits may include: (1) bacteriological sampling of aircraft water system; (2) reviews and audits of records pertaining to operations and maintenance such as log entries, disinfection and flushing procedures, and sampling results; (3) observation of procedures involving handling of finished water, watering point selection, boarding of water, operation, disinfection and flushing, and general maintenance and self-inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-inspection frequency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Air carriers or their representatives must perform a self-inspection of all water system components for each aircraft water system no less frequently than once every 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline to address deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must address any deficiency identified during compliance audits or routine self-inspections within 90 days of identification of the deficiency, or where identified during extended or heavy maintenance, before the aircraft is put back into service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes deficiencies in design, construction, operation, maintenance, or administration, and any failure or malfunction of any system component that could cause unacceptable risk to health or affect reliable delivery of safe drinking water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental treatment unit acceptability and installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplemental drinking water treatment units installed onboard existing or new aircraft must be acceptable to FAA and FDA, and must be installed, operated, and maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's plans and specifications and FAA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental treatment performance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Water supplemental treatment and production equipment must produce water that meets the standards prescribed in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated violations constituting noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An air carrier is in violation of this subpart when any of the following occur:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Fails to perform any of the requirements in accordance with § 141.803 or § 141.804. (b) Has an E. coli-positive sample in any monitoring period (routine and repeat samples are used in this determination). (c) Fails to provide notification to passengers and crew per § 141.805. (d) Fails to comply with reporting and recordkeeping requirements of this subpart. (e) Fails to conduct a self-inspection or address a deficiency per § 141.808. (f) Fails to develop a coliform sampling plan per § 141.802, or fails to have and follow an operations and maintenance plan included in an FAA-accepted program per § 141.804.
